title: Prioritization Playbook: Key-Account Intake Matrix & Roadmap Signals
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a repeatable, defensible process that converts inbound requests and escalations from strategic customers into prioritization signals for the public roadmap. The deliverable is a lightweight intake matrix + scoring rubric, a standardized intake form, and playbook pages for PMs, AE/CS, and Eng on how to triage, commit, and communicate decisions to top accounts.
success_criteria: 1) Intake form adopted by 3 pilot AE teams within 3 weeks. 2) >90% of pilot requests have a documented score and disposition in the ticket. 3) Reduction in ad-hoc escalations by 30% in first quarter after rollout. 4) Executive-visible dashboard showing expected customer revenue at-risk vs committed roadmap items.
scope: Covers inbound product requests and escalations from named accounts (Top 50). Excludes purely supportable incidents and infra SRE tickets. Includes playbooks for Priority Commit (short-term SLA) and Backlog Funding (long-term roadmap).
proposed_process: 1) Intake: CS/AE complete canonical form (Confluence + Airtable) capturing: customer ID, ARR tier, impact scenario, reproducible example, requested timeline, regulatory constraints. 2) Scoring: auto-calc score from weighted factors (revenue, legal risk, deliverability, strategic alignment). 3) Triage cadence: weekly Product Ops queue review with AE/CS reps + ENG rotation. 4) Outcome taxonomy: Commit, Fund, Evaluate, Reject with templated responses and SLAs. 5) Roadmap mapping: map Commit items into quarterly rollouts with canary cohort and rollback criteria.
tradeoffs: - Speed vs fairness: fast commits risk favoritism; we mitigate with objective weights and mandatory documentation. - Engineering headroom vs customer SLAs: we limit Priority Commits to a bounded quarterly capacity (configurable). - Visibility vs noise: expose only 'Commit' and 'Funded' items to exec dashboard to avoid roadmap churn.
